title: Spline-Based Transformations knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the central idea of “Spline-Based Transformations”?
options: The method always performs better than a simple baseline, regardless of the task.

The method removes the need to inspect data quality or define an evaluation strategy.
questions.answer_key: Spline-Based Transformations is part of Data Preprocessing and Feature Transformation. Define the task, inspect the inputs, choose a simple reference approach, and test the result on representative examples before drawing conclusions.
questions.explanation: The lesson frames the topic this way: Spline-Based Transformations is part of Data Preprocessing and Feature Transformation. Define the task, inspect the inputs, choose a simple reference approach, and test the result on representative examples before drawing conclusions. The other options make unsupported guarantees.

questions.answer_key: Name the inputs, assumptions, and output for Basis functions and nonlinear relationships; then test it on representative data.
questions.explanation: Define the input, output, assumptions, and evidence needed. For Basis functions and nonlinear relationships, a small representative check is more useful than blind tuning.

questions.prompt: What conclusion is appropriately cautious after trying “Spline-Based Transformations”?
options: A single successful run proves fairness, robustness, and production readiness.
A higher training score alone proves generalization to unseen data.
An internal estimator score replaces domain review and operational monitoring.

questions.answer_key: A successful small example is useful evidence about that example, but generalization, risks, and limitations still need separate checks.
questions.explanation: A demonstration only supports conclusions within its scope. Evaluate representative unseen cases and report limitations before production use.
